name: Harmony Today — earthy / outdoor-ed, DARK
note: Dark alternate of tokens.json, matching board 3a in School Dashboard.dc.html exactly. Same role names, same hue families — only the lightness order is inverted: the page is deep forest ink, cards sit a step lighter, accents rise so they hold on a dark ground. `maps_to` names the light token each value replaces, so a theme swap is key-for-key by NAME, not by hex.
swap_rule: Every name in tokens.json.color exists here. No geometry, spacing, radius, or type value changes between themes.

card-alt.use: footer zone — darker than paper, not lighter

card-sunken.use: chip fills inside a card (the light theme uses paper here)

garden.use: primary action fill, links, accent bars

garden-deep.use: wordmark, card headings — INVERTED ROLE: on dark this is the lighter of the pair

clay-lift.use: accent bar / tag stroke where clay must read against a dark card

clay-ink.use: WhatsApp chip text, shARK tag text

on-clay.use: text on a clay fill — stays near-white in both themes

sun-ink.use: text on sun — unchanged; sun stays a light fill

bezel.use: device frame only, not part of the UI

gradient.note: The hero deepens rather than brightens on dark; its near-white text carries the emphasis.

role_inversions: garden-deep and garden swap perceptual position: on light, garden-deep is the darker emphasis; on dark it is the lighter. Keep garden-deep for wordmark and headings and garden for fills and actions — the names describe role, not lightness.
card-alt is DARKER than paper on dark (#151B14 vs #1C231A). The footer zone recedes in both themes; it just changes direction.
Chip fills invert too: the light theme drops chips onto `paper` inside a `card`; the dark theme needs the extra `card-sunken` step because paper is now darker than card.

sun and clay keep their light-theme hex values. Both stay light fills with dark or near-white text, which is what keeps alerts reading identically across themes. clay-lift and clay-ink exist only for the cases where clay is a 3px bar or small text on a dark card.
sky and iris also keep their light-theme hex as accent bars; their chip fills and text invert.

contrast.standard: WCAG AA for text (4.5:1 body, 3:1 for display >= 24px)
notes: ink #EDF2E7 on card #2C3B29 — comfortable AA for body and display.
ink-muted #8FA388 on card is the floor for captions; do not use it for body copy.
ink-ghost #5F7059 is decorative only — struck-through listings and the update stamp, never load-bearing text.
garden #3F7A43 from the light theme FAILS on a dark card. It is replaced by #72B36E for links/actions and #9BD094 for headings. Never carry the light green across.

unchanged_from_light.type: identical — no size or weight changes between themes

border.note: Widths and roles identical; only the color tokens resolve differently.

unchanged_from_light.shadow: still none — separation stays border plus fill. Dark themes invite glow; do not add it.
unchanged_from_light.event-kind-color: identical mapping (break/holiday/no_school → sun, early_release → clay, conference → iris, event → sky, shark → clay, milestone → garden)
unchanged_from_light.source-chip: identical mapping and geometry; fills and text resolve to the dark values above

usage.selection: Theme is a per-display build choice, not a user toggle. Suggested: wall tablet runs dark (it lives on a wall through the evening); phone and laptop follow prefers-color-scheme.
usage.emoji: Unchanged and untreated — they carry their own color and read on both grounds.
usage.sponsor_logos: Logos supplied for the light theme may need a light plate behind them on dark. Add `logo_needs_plate: true` per entry in sponsors.json rather than filtering the image.
